title: With 4K/240fps slow-mo, this upcoming flagship could blow rivals out of the water
summary: vivo's upcoming X500 Pro could offer better slow-mo and wider dynamic range than any other phone on the market.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR vivo has started officially teasing the X500 series, featuring its upcoming camera-centric flagships. The vivo X500 Pro will use a custom Sony sensor that offers 17 stops of dynamic range, producing well-lit shadows even with bright highlights. The Pro is also claimed to be the first phone to capture slow-mo at 4K@240p. It’s been mere months since we took a good look at vivo’s colossal Ultra camera masquerading as a phone with one of the farthest-reaching zoom lenses . Come September, major phone giants will keep us busy with new releases. Among them, vivo is set to launch a new flagship camera phone with some serious upgrades previously unseen on phone cameras. In a recent Weibo post , vivo’s product manager Han Boxiao revealed camera upgrades coming for the upcoming vivo X500 series. Boxiao writes that while previous devices have aced at phone photography, the upcoming X500 series “aims to take mobile video to another level.” When I tested the X300 Pro from earlier this year, I found it to outpace the iPhone 17 Pro in video , and the upcoming phones could take a major leap, as the representative suggests.

title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: I want to love the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, but one silly change is stopping me
summary: To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold roughly 1mm thinner, Google made this compromise.
body: Before the Pixel 11 Pro Fold became official, I shared a wishlist of changes I wanted Google to make for its next foldable. To my surprise, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers many of the upgrades I needed to take Google foldables seriously again. It’s thinner and lighter, has slimmer bezels and better screens, and supports faster 25W Qi2 wireless charging. However, Google also made an unexpected change to the Pixel 11 Pro Fold that I can’t overlook. To make the Pixel 11 Pro Fold about 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, compromises had to be made. The one you probably noticed is the smaller 4,806mAh battery capacity, but that isn’t the one I care about.

title: Google fixed this Google Maps issue on mobile, but it’s back now on Android Auto
summary: The traffic view works on phones but disappears behind the wheel.
body: TL;DR Traffic lines are disappearing from Google Maps on Android Auto for some users. The issue appears limited to Android Auto, not Maps on phones. Some users say the problem started after the Immersive Navigation update arrived. Google Maps users really can’t seem to catch a break lately. Not long after Google fixed a bug that made color-coded traffic lines disappear across Android, iOS, and desktop, the same issue has now appeared in Android Auto. Several users in the Android Auto community and on Reddit are reporting that Google Maps no longer shows the familiar green, yellow, orange, and red traffic lines on their car’s screen. The problem appears to be limited to Android Auto, with affected users reporting that traffic displays normally when they open Google Maps directly on their phones.

title: Foo Fighters Play First-Ever Hollywood Bowl Show With LA Philharmonic
summary: It marked the band's first time playing the venue in its more than three decades together.
body: Foo Fighters paused their Take Cover Tour for a one-off performance with the Los Angeles Philharmonic at the Hollywood Bowl on Saturday (Aug. 22), joining conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the Youth Orchestra Los Angeles for a 15-song set honoring Dudamel’s final season with the Phil. It marked the band’s first time playing the venue in its more than three decades together. Backed by full orchestra and choir, the band moved through a set blending hits with several deep cuts rarely aired live. The night opened with “Times Like These” before running through “All My Life,” “The Pretender,” “Walk,” “My Hero,” “Learn to Fly,” “The Sky Is a Neighborhood” and “Run.” The rarities came in a cluster: “I Should Have Known,” from 2011’s Wasting Light , got its first performance since 2012; “Razor,” from 2005’s In Your Honor , returned for the first time since 2006; and “Home,” from 2007’s Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace , got its first live outing since 2007. The band also revived “A320,” a deep cut from the 1998 Godzil…

title: You’re not alone: Claude is down right now (Updated: Services restored)
summary: Claude's having some issues this Monday morning.
body: Credit: Mitja Rutnik / Android Authority TL;DR Claude is experiencing an outage right now, with users reporting problems across the service. Anthropic says it has identified the cause of elevated errors affecting multiple Claude models and is working on a fix. The company has yet to provide a timeline for when the issues will be fully resolved. Update: August 24, 2026 (5:15 AM ET): Anthropic has updated its Status page, indicating that issues with Claude, particularly with the Fable 5, Mythos 5, and Opus 5 models, were resolved as of 8:30 AM UTC (4:00 AM ET). The issues lasted roughly three hours, according to Anthropic. You should now be able to use Claude on the web, mobile, desktop, or through the API as usual.

title: New OnePlus 16 leak gives us another clue about what the US will miss out on
summary: It's a shame that it won't launch in the US.
body: TL;DR A new leak suggests that the OnePlus 16 will come with the thinnest bezels of any OnePlus phone. It also states that it will feature a “custom-designed screen.” The OnePlus 16 will have one of the best front-facing designs, per the leak. We’ve seen a bunch of OnePlus 16 leaks over the last couple of months, and with each one, the upcoming Android flagship looks more and more promising. Following leaks of a 9,000mAh battery and a true 165Hz display , a new leak suggests the phone’s screen could be excellent in both performance and looks. According to a Weibo post by leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS), the OnePlus 16 will come with the thinnest bezels on any OnePlus phone so far and a display experience to match. The leak doesn’t state exactly how thin the bezels could be, but states they will be “around this narrow .”

title: Unannounced phones land on Motorola’s Android 17 update list, but actual ones miss out
summary: Lenovo skipped over recent Edge and Moto G models for Android 17 update eligiblity.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR Lenovo’s Android 17 list features unannounced models, such as the Motorola Edge 70 Neo and Edge 70 Plus, while omitting current 2024 and 2025 phones. Omitted devices include several phones from the Motorola Edge 50 lineup, the Razr 2024, the Moto G56 5G, and the Moto G75 5G, despite earlier multi-year update promises. There are also inconsistencies in the official Android 17 update list, such as duplicate entries for the Motorola Edge 60, raising a lot of questions about the overall list. Earlier this month, Lenovo published a list of Motorola phones confirmed to receive the Android 17 update . While the update included plenty of phones across Motorola’s expansive device portfolio, it also excluded several prominent, relatively recent models that should have made the cut for Android 17 . When Lenovo published the Android 17 eligibility list, users on Reddit and in the comments section of our article mentioned that the following phones were missing:

title: Pixel 11 owners can’t play Genshin Impact, but a fix is on the way
summary: Genshin Impact unplayable on your new Pixel 11 phone? You're not alone, but a fix is coming.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel 11 series owners are reporting that Genshin Impact is unplayable due to severe graphical problems. The developer reportedly said that PowerVR GPUs don’t meet its minimum requirements. Google has apparently confirmed the issue while noting that a fix will arrive in an upcoming game update. The Google Pixel 11 phones are powered by a Tensor G6 processor, which uses a PowerVR GPU. Unfortunately, you can’t play Genshin Impact on these new phones. Thankfully, a solution is in the works. Pixel 11 series owners reported severe graphical issues when trying to run Genshin Impact on their phones. These problems made the game unplayable as a result. The issue has also been flagged via Google’s Issue Tracker .

title: Crazy report reveals Exynos 2700 could outperform Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro
summary: Just FYI, Samsung reportedly conducted these tests itself.
body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly tested its Exynos 2700 chip against the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Gen 6 Pro. According to the tests, the Exynos 2700 performed 9.5% better than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 in Geekbench 6.5. It also performed 5% better in gaming and 24% better in gaming under low-power conditions. It’s no secret that the Exynos 2700 is coming and will power many phones in the upcoming Galaxy S27 series , at least in some regions. However, if you’re wondering whether an Exynos chipset in your next Galaxy flagship means poor gaming performance and thermal throttling, Samsung may have good news. According to a report from South Korean outlet SEDaily , citing industry sources, the Exynos 2700 outperformed the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro in an in-house evaluation by Samsung. The report further claims that the Exynos chip beat Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chip in multiple categories.

title: Sony’s Xperia 10 VIII just leaked ahead of its big reveal
summary: We're still searching for what changed.
body: TL;DR A leaked image appears to give us an early look at the Sony Xperia 10 VIII ahead of its August 25 unveiling. The phone looks remarkably similar to the Xperia 10 VII, retaining the flat back, horizontal dual-camera bar, and side-mounted fingerprint reader. Leaks also point to the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 and 8GB of RAM, leaving us wondering where Sony’s biggest upgrades will come from. A few days ago, we reported that Sony could unveil the Xperia 10 VIII this week. We may not have to wait until the event to see what it looks like, though. Android Headlines has now shared an image that appears to show Sony’s Xperia 10 VIII out in the wild. The image shows a woman holding the phone and looking at the screen. More importantly, we get a clear look at the back. The phone appears to have a white finish with a slight green tint, and if you’ve seen the Xperia 10 VII before, you’ll probably notice something immediately: Sony hasn’t changed much.

title: GrapheneOS’ Motorola plans include 7 years of updates, foldables, and more
summary: Graphene just can't stop talking about its Motorola plans, and we're all ears.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS says it plans to support both regular Motorola phones as well as Razr foldables. The project says next-gen Snapdragon chips will bring the MTE and secure element improvements needed for GrapheneOS. GrapheneOS also requires a seven-year update commitment on devices. GrapheneOS has revealed a lot more about its plans to expand beyond Pixel phones to Motorola devices. The project has now confirmed that its Motorola partnership will eventually cover both traditional smartphones as well as Razr foldables. The privacy-focused Android operating system says its initial focus will be a regular, non-folding flagship, with the first supported Motorola devices expected to arrive in 2027.

title: The Wallflowers Announce First-Ever Australian Tour
summary: The band will perform 1996 breakthrough Bringing Down the Horse in full for its 30th anniversary.
body: The Wallflowers will play Australia for the first time, announcing a five-date tour presented by Love Police to mark the 30th anniversary of their breakthrough album, Bringing Down the Horse . The band will perform the album in full at every show. The tour opens at Melbourne’s Palais Theatre on Friday, Dec. 4, followed by Thirroul’s Anita’s Theatre on Dec. 5, Sydney’s Liberty Hall on Dec. 6, Brisbane’s Fortitude Music Hall on Dec. 8 and Adelaide’s Hindley Street Music Hall on Dec. 9. A promoter presale begins Wednesday, Aug. 26, with general tickets on sale Friday, Aug. 28. Bringing Down the Horse , released May 21, 1996, peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and was certified quadruple platinum in the U.S.; in Australia it went gold and reached No. 9 on the ARIA chart. Lead single “One Headlight” became the band’s signature hit, topping Billboard’s Mainstream Rock, Modern Rock and Triple-A airplay charts simultaneously and winning two Grammy Awards in 1998 for best rock song and best rock performance by a duo or group with vocals. It later landed at No. 58 on Rolling Stone’s list of the 100 greatest pop songs. The a…

title: QMusic Confirms Kristy Ellis as New CEO
summary: Ellis, who was appointed interim CEO of the trade body in April, steps into the position on a permanent basis, following a nationwide recruitment process.
body: BRISBANE, Australia — The search is over. Kristy Ellis is the new CEO of QMusic . Ellis, who was appointed interim CEO of the trade body in April, steps into the position on a permanent basis, following a nationwide recruitment process. Moving forward, Ellis will oversee the association as it drives sector growth and delivers key industry programs and events, which include the BIGSOUND summit and showcase event and the Queensland Music Awards ( QMAs ). Ellis boasts more than two decades’ experience in the creative industries, sports, major events and commercial management, with previous role at AFC Women’s Asian Cup, Queensland Rugby Union (Queensland Reds), TEDxBrisbane, and as a board member for Ballet Theatre Queensland. “It is a privilege to lead QMusic permanently at such a dynamic time for Queensland music,” she comments in a statement, issued Monday morning (Aug. 24) local time. “Over the past several months, working alongside our team, members, and key stakeholders, it has become even clearer how much talent and opportunity exist across our state’s music ecosystem. “My commitment is to deliver both operational continuity and fresh …

title: I canceled Netflix a year ago — here’s the unexpected alternative I finally stuck with
summary: I never expected to find myself fawning over Apple TV.
body: I have been in a streaming rut for some time. I canceled my Netflix subscription last year after growing increasingly dissatisfied with the platform. However, finding a Netflix alternative that sticks, especially in a market with limited competition, has been a challenge. I cycled through a few options and couldn’t find one that really kept me hooked or made me feel like I was getting my money’s worth. And the platform I finally settled on — Apple TV — was the last one I expected to capture my loyalty.

title: Google’s foldable strategy is broken, and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold proves it
summary: This Fold left me cold.
body: Google launched the Pixel 11 series last week, and as someone with a soft spot for foldables, there was one phone I immediately wanted to learn more about: the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. I’ve spent a fair amount of time with foldables lately, especially after using Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra . So, I was genuinely curious to see how Google would respond. Would the new Pixel Fold finally feel like a good alternative? Would Google fix some of the things that held back last year’s model? More importantly, would it give me a reason to pick it over Samsung’s polished foldables?

title: 6 Android phones with microSD card slots you can still buy in 2026
summary: Say "no" to overpriced storage.
body: The smartphone industry is finally feeling the full effect of RAMageddon in 2026, as prices have shot up across the board due to rising memory costs. Brands are no longer able (or unwilling) to absorb the higher cost of components, so this is now passed on to us, the consumers. Smartphones with higher RAM and storage now command a steep premium, even more so than before. Thankfully, a small segment of smartphones still exists that has a solution for the storage crisis — the microSD card slot. It’s mostly entry-level and a few mid-range Android phones that still support the microSD card, but there are some good models to choose from. Flagship Android phones have largely done away with this feature, except for a few specialized models that aren’t widely available in the US.

title: Pixel Camera 11 debuts refreshed quick access controls and a handy Launch mode
summary: The upgrade is easy to miss.
body: TL;DR Pixel Camera 11 gets redesigned Quick access controls with sleek, dial-like sliders for settings such as focus, exposure, ISO, and shutter speed. The new dials are hidden by default and only appear after tapping the viewfinder, making the feature easy to miss. A new Launch mode lets Pixel 11 owners open the camera directly to Video or Magic Capture instead of the default Photo mode. With the new Pixel 11 series, Google’s releasing its updated Pixel Camera 11 app, including redesigned Quick access sliders. Let’s take a look at what these do, and how you’ll access them. Google has given its Quick access camera controls a major redesign in Pixel Camera 11, but there’s a catch: these controls are hidden by default. And even when you dig through menus to enable them, using the controls isn’t exactly intuitive.

title: Google is starting to show ads on Pixel phones — here’s how to turn them off
summary: Ads suck, but at least you can get rid of this one.
body: One of the things people love most about a Pixel is the lack of bloatware and ads. That’s still largely true, but Google has started to give in to temptation. After the launch of the Pixel 11 series , many users, myself included, started receiving ads for the new phone on our older Pixels. It’s the sort of thing we’ve come to expect from Samsung, but not so much Google.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro is setting a dangerous precedent for Android upgrades
summary: Old Pixels are going to pay the price.
body: The Pixel 11 Pro announcement was frustrating for many reasons. I hated that Google raised the price of its flagship phones while also reducing RAM on the Pro base models. While I don’t believe 12GB of RAM will noticeably hinder the user experience, it’s disappointing to pay more for less — regardless of the circumstances. Unfortunately, there is more to the Pixel 11 Pro than meets the eye. The phone outlines precisely how Google plans to get you to upgrade more frequently, and it has nothing to do with actually needing to buy a new device.

title: Whatever you do, don’t buy a Pixel 11 right now if you already have a Pixel 10
summary: The Pixel 11 series looks great, but the Pixel 10 hasn't aged much in just a year.
body: The Pixel 11 series is official, and with it comes the Tensor G6 processor, a slightly upgraded camera package, and plenty of new AI and software tweaks. As tempting as the Pixel 11 might be, it’s also pretty familiar to its predecessor.

title: I’m quitting Kindle, and Amazon’s new DRM update proves why you should too
summary: I’m finally ready to leave the Kindle world behind.
body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.

title: Your Verizon Disney Plus, Hulu, and ESPN Plus perks are about to cost more
summary: Most Verizon Disney bundle perks are going up, but this $15 plan is staying put.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Verizon has announced that it will adjust prices for its Disney Plus, Hulu, and ESPN Plus plan perks. All perks are getting a price bump, except the $15 Legacy Disney Bundle. The changes will go into effect on September 17, 2026. Recently, NBCUniversal raised the price of Peacock subscription plans . Unfortunately, every tier on the platform was hit with a bump of $1.00 or more. On the heels of that price hike, Verizon is preparing to raise the price of its Disney Plus, Hulu, and ESPN Plus streaming perks. But at least one plan is safe from the change. According to a Verizon FAQ page , the internet provider will be adjusting the prices for its Disney Plus, Hulu, and ESPN Plus plan perks. Verizon explains, “As our partners at Disney invest in new content and adjust the rates of their services, we periodically need to adjust our perk rates.”

title: Google is giving you more control over your shared photo location data
summary: Android's Photo Picker is adding a location data toggle for shared photos.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR Google is introducing a new Photo Picker API that allows users to choose if location data is included with the photos they share. If the user agrees to share location data with an app, they won’t be asked again for that app. Users will be able to revoke access or regrant access by tapping on the location info button in the bottom right corner of the Photo Picker UI. By default, Android’s Photo Picker strips location data (EXIF data) from the photos you choose to share with apps. While this is great for those who care deeply about privacy, certain apps rely on EXIF data (for non-invasive reasons) to function properly. Back in June, we spotted code that suggested Google was working on giving you more granular control over your location data in the Photo Picker UI. The company has now confirmed that the change will be rolling out soon. In a Reddit post , Mishaal Rahman, who manages community engagement for Android at Google, revealed that the company is introducing a new Photo Picker API to address a “common pain point” app developers have with how the Android Photo Picker currently behaves. While the previous API removes location data…

title: Redeeming Google Play Points could win you a vintage Spider-Man comic worth crazy money
summary: Play Points payments possibly procure prized Peter Parker periodical
body: TL;DR Google is running a sweepstakes with prizes that include a prized vintage Spider-Man comic and trips to New York Comic Con. You can enter the sweepstakes by redeeming Play Points; each point redeemed is one entry. The sweepstakes is running now through September 14. Google is running a sweepstakes for the next few weeks, and participants stand to win some valuable prizes. Redeeming Play Points between now and the middle of September puts you in the running to win a trip to New York Comic Con or a vintage Spider-Man comic valued at more than $70,000, among other prizes. Google announced the sweepstakes in a blog post today. The most interesting prize on offer is one sealed, graded copy of Marvel’s Amazing Fantasy #15, an issue from 1962 that marked the hero’s first appearance. And four entrants will win a trip for two to New York Comic Con, including flights and a four-night stay in Times Square.

title: Google Messages group chat invite links look nearly ready to go
summary: Google's making it easier to get people into your group chats.
body: TL;DR We saw that Google Messages was working on adding group chat invite links last year. That feature still isn’t generally available, but we’ve managed to get invite links working in a recent beta version of Messages. This makes it seem like group chat invite links could go live in Google Messages any time now. Way back in May of last year, we spotted that Google was working to implement invite links for group chats in Google Messages. The feature was incomplete at the time, and it’s still not accessible by default — but now, we’ve managed to get these invite links up and running. The latest iteration of the in-development invite links feature is fundamentally the same as what we saw last year. Once it’s rolled out, you’ll be able to share text links or QR codes that others can use to join your group chats. The biggest new development here is that the system is now functional: in our recent testing, we were able to generate working invite links.

title: Need a flatter wallet tracker? The new Eufy SmartTrack Card E40 is already down to $24.99
summary: The SmartTrack Card E40 drops to $24.99 in its best deal since launch, with Apple Find My and Google Find Hub support.
body: Lost wallets are a pain, and bulky trackers are not much better when they make your pocket or card holder feel stuffed. The new Eufy SmartTrack Card E40 is built for that exact problem, and there’s a good Amazon deal on it right now. See the deal at Amazon

title: Is Dropbox down for you? Here’s what’s going on (Update)
summary: Dropbox is currently working on a fix.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Dropbox is experiencing an outage. The company confirms that the website is down, but says that the mobile app is still working. The team is working on a fix. Update: August 21, 2026 (4:24 PM ET): Dropbox status site says that the incident causing the outage has been resolved. However, it still marks the website as having partially degraded service. Original article: August 21, 2026 (10:20 AM ET): If you’re running into trouble with Dropbox this morning, don’t worry, there’s nothing wrong on your end. You can rest easy knowing that you’re not alone, as other users are also unable to use the service. Here’s what’s going on.

title: Pixel Watch 5 factory images are here with one convenient change
summary: Google has consolidated both cellular and Wi-Fi versions into one build.
body: TL;DR Alongside the Pixel 11 series, Google has published factory images of the Pixel Watch 5. However, unlike in years past, there’s only one image for the cellular and Wi-Fi variants of the Pixel Watch 5. Flashing factory images on the Pixel Watch 5 will be as tricky as on the Pixel Watch 4, as it still requires an invite-only debug adapter distributed by Google. The Pixel 11 series is gradually reaching customers beginning this week, and Google has obliged by publishing factory images for these smartphones . At the same time, the company has also posted factory images for the Pixel Watch 5. However, there’s one crucial change with the new smartwatch. Much like last year, Google offers the Pixel Watch 5 in both 4G LTE and Bluetooth/Wi-Fi variants. While it has traditionally published separate images for these variants, the manufacturer is offering only one build this time (via 9to5Google ).

title: Survey suggests this is the slowest carrier if you have a cheap phone
summary: There's good news for T-Mobile subscribers with cheap phones, though.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Verizon recorded the biggest gap in cellular speeds between flagship and budget phones, according to a new survey. T-Mobile had the smallest gap in speeds between high-end and cheap phones. The survey also showed that Verizon recorded the lowest average speed for cheap phones in general. The latest flagship Android phones are often equipped with blazing-fast cellular speeds owing to more advanced modems. But a new survey suggests that the speed gap between flagship and budget phones can also be accentuated by the carrier. A survey by Recon Analytics (h/t: PhoneArena ) yielded over 4,300 speed tests across US carriers. The survey found that flagship phones often had faster speeds than budget devices on the same network. That isn’t a surprise on its own, as high-end phones tend to get faster modems.

title: I tried Android 17 QPR2 Beta 3 — these 3 features completely changed my Pixel
summary: Android 17 QPR2 keeps getting better and better.
body: In the midst of all the Pixel 11 hubbub last week, you might have missed another bit of Google news that went under the radar. Just a couple of days after announcing the Pixel 11 lineup, Google rolled out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 3 . Android 17 betas have been hit-and-miss with user-facing changes. Plus, with a thrilling name like “Android 17 QPR2 Beta 3,” I wouldn’t blame you for thinking this was a pretty boring beta release focused on bug fixes and other optimizations.

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the Pixel 11 Pro XL
summary: It's not an easy decision this year.
body: The Pixel 11 Pro XL’s reveal brought with it more questions than answers. Google’s new flagship is a mixed bag, with some needed enhancements but also an unfortunate downgrade. It’s a phone that is harder to justify this year, as Google has raised prices, which will give some buyers the impression they are paying more for less. It’s not an easy decision, even for hardcore Pixel fans. Smartphones have gotten more expensive across the board, but Google is now on the same playing field as everyone else, and buyers will demand results. If you’re on the fence about buying a new Pixel 11 Pro XL, here are five Android alternatives that can win you over instead.

title: From design to peel-ready sticker in a single go, the Liene PixCut S1 all-in-one printer and cutter is the ideal back-to-school gadget
summary: Ideal for all your back-to-school customized stickers, labels, and printing needs.
body: Back-to-school usually means two things: a shopping list and things that need labels and stickers. Whether you’re looking to add name tags to your or your kids’ supplies, make planner stickers, or want to add a personalized touch to your laptop lid or dorm room, it can be quite a time-consuming project. Creating a custom sticker sheet typically means designing on one screen, printing on another device, then carrying that sheet to a separate cutter to trace and slice by hand. And any misstep along the way means going right back to the start. The Liene PixCut S1 is the company’s attempt to combine that entire chain into a single device. Liene has spent 700 days developing, testing, and refining its all-in-one printer and cutter, just in time for the start of the new school year. With the PixCut S1 Starter Kit, you have the perfect tool for making name labels, planner stickers, locker decor, and more. Here’s what you need to know.

title: Google’s new Tap to Share feature on the Pixel 11 is incredible. Here’s how to use it
summary: Just a tap away.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority Google has introduced a much more intuitive way to use Quick Share with the Pixel 11 series. Called Tap to Share, the feature lets you initiate a Quick Share connection simply by bringing the tops of two compatible Android phones together. If that sounds familiar, it’s because we’ve seen Apple do the very same thing for a while now. Google’s version works pretty much the same way, and the company has even made some hardware changes to the Pixel 11 series to support it.

title: YouTube Premium could get another price hike just months after the last one
summary: Reports point to higher Premium prices and another hit to your monthly bill.
body: TL;DR YouTube Premium could be getting another price hike just months after April’s increase, according to reports from subscribers across Europe. Individual and family plans could both become more expensive, with some users already receiving emails detailing higher monthly prices. The reports are not yet official, and it’s unclear if or when the increases will reach the US and other markets. It’s only been a few months since YouTube Premium’s price in the US went up , and now we’re getting wind of yet another looming price increase. While April 2026’s hike raised the subscription price from $13.99 to $15.99, fresh reports suggest YouTube could also increase subscription prices in Europe by the end of October 2026. According to reports on Reddit and the ResetEra forum , YouTube could be preparing a price hike just a few months after rolling out new prices across its Premium plans in the US. The change will likely come in the next couple of months and will affect both individual and family plans across various European countries.

title: RayNeo wants its new iO Smart Glasses to be the reason you stop reaching for your phone
summary: The company's answer to screen fatigue is another screen right in your face.
body: TL;DR RayNeo’s new iO Smart Glasses put a tiny MicroLED display and AI assistant into regular-looking 33g frames, letting you glance at information without reaching for your phone. The glasses can surface notifications, schedules and weather, translate text in 40 languages, capture voice notes and even act as a hands-free teleprompter. The iO launches September 4 for $479, with up to 48 hours of typical battery life; a $529 bundle includes a charging case. Screens are a major part of our life, but that doesn’t mean screen fatigue isn’t real. We carry our phone everywhere with us, and when we’re not out and about, we’re staring at other screens. That’s a problem that AR glasses-maker RayNeo is trying to solve with its new iO Smart Glasses. First things first: Yes, the glasses themselves have a screen, but that’s not necessarily a contradiction. RayNeo’s aim is that its new glasses’ tiny display is all you’ll need to quickly glance at information, eliminating the urge for you to unnecessarily reach for your phone and make your tech interactions overall less disruptive.

title: RayNeo targets movie lovers with GT and GT Max AR glasses and a new Pocket TV Pro Google TV streamer
summary: The Pocket TV Pro is locked to RayNeo AR glasses though, so don't get your hopes too high up.
body: TL;DR RayNeo has announced the RayNeo GT and GT Max AR glasses featuring dual 1080p, 120Hz micro-OLED displays, dual-chip architecture, and Bang & Olufsen quad speakers. The RayNeo GT will cost you $299 at launch, while the RayNeo GT Max will cost you $399. These can be paired with the new RayNeo Pocket TV Pro, which is a RayNeo-specific Google TV streaming puck, to deliver Dolby Vision content. RayNeo has been making AR glasses for a while now, with its RayNeo Air 4 Pro glasses going global earlier this year at CES 2026. The company is back with a new cinema-grade pair, the RayNeo GT and GT Max, alongside the Pocket TV Pro streaming puck and the RayNeo iO Smart glasses . RayNeo GT and RayNeo GT Max

title: GrapheneOS’ first Motorola phones will be flagships that cost more than Pixels
summary: If you were hoping for GrapheneOS' first Moto phones to be cheap, you're all out of luck.
body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS says its first Motorola phones will arrive in 2027 as high-end flagships that will cost more than Pixel phones. The platform says lower-end devices will take longer to qualify because Qualcomm’s cheaper chipsets don’t currently offer the same level of security and long-term software support. GrapheneOS also plans to have its Motorola builds ready alongside major Android releases, but it will need to host and maintain its own AOSP repositories. GrapheneOS is getting ready to expand beyond Google Pixel phones in 2027, but the platform has now revealed that its first Motorola devices won’t be affordable alternatives. The privacy-focused Android project says its initial Motorola devices will be flagships with higher-end hardware and higher prices than comparable Pixels.

title: Google Photos users are overwhelmingly asking for better cleanup options
summary: A landslide result in our latest poll suggests the current cleanup tools aren't cutting it for most of you.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority Google Photos does a lot of things right, which is just as well since many of us sleepwalked into using it and are now somewhat reliant on it. But the quality of phone cameras in 2026 means the standard 15GB of free storage — less if you don’t want to share your phone number — feels like almost nothing, and at some point, you might decide you’d quite like some of that space back. Google does offer tools to help you reclaim those gigabytes, but we recently asked readers whether the whole process should be easier. My colleague Megan Ellis recently shared a handful of tips and tricks for freeing up Google Photos storage after doing some serious housekeeping on her own library. With more than 47,000 backed-up items, she managed to claw back around 23GB by using Google’s existing cleanup tools and a few more hands-on methods. The experience also exposed some obvious limitations, especially the lack of a straightforward duplicate-photo finder, so we asked readers whether Google needs to make the job easier via a poll in her article.

title: This Galaxy S26 FE leak just exposed the full color palette
summary: The Galaxy S26 FE just got completely exposed by this leak.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR A leak has shared new renders of the Galaxy S26 FE. The leak showcases the device in three color options. title: Some Pixel phones have forgotten how to Flip to Shhh
summary: The easiest way to silence notifications on your Pixel might just be broken.
body: TL;DR Pixel’s Flip to Shhh gesture has stopped working for some users, with the feature either becoming impossible to enable or disappearing from Settings entirely. Updating the Digital Wellbeing app appears to fix the issue for some users, although Google hasn’t confirmed the connection and the fix isn’t universal. Some users say the problem persists or returns after updating, and we’ve reached out to Google for more information. Your Pixel phone comes with a handy little trick for those moments when you just can’t be bothered — it lets you turn your phone face down on a flat surface to silence all notifications. Called Flip to Shhh, it was released with the Pixel 3 all the way back in 2018. Up until recently, the gesture-based feature has largely worked as intended — that, however, is no longer the case for some. Over the last couple weeks, several disgruntled users have taken to Reddit to air their frustration with the feature. Flip to Shhh had suddenly stopped working for many with no clear reason.

title: Google’s working with your carrier to fix RCS in Messages
summary: Hopefully this glitch will soon be a thing of the past.
body: TL;DR Android users have been reporting some frustrating RCS problems with Google Messages. Users suggested a number of fixes, but they don’t appear to work for everyone. Google now confirms that it’s working with carriers to developer a proper solution. RCS represents the next generation of text messaging, finally delivering many of the features users were craving for years, like threads and reactions. But all that complexity also feels like it’s made things a bit fragile, and sometimes it seems that we can’t go more that a few weeks without hearing about a new RCS glitch . Most recently, that’s one that’s involved error code 3100 , and appears to largely impact users setting up new devices or switching carriers. Today, Google gives us an update on progress towards sorting things out. As you may remember, we already looked at a number of potential solutions and work-arounds, and while some users did report success, it was clear that the same approach wasn’t working for everyone. Especially with something like RCS that can rely so much on external systems, that’s a situation that can feel incredibly frustrating. But that’s also why we’re relieved to now hear that Google’s on the c…

title: Gemini for Home sharpens Spotify control, lighting tweaks, and message broadcasts
summary: Gemini for Home is getting a trio of improvements.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini for Home is getting better at recognizing songs, artists, and playlists on Spotify. The voice assistant is also getting better at controlling the color temperature of your smart lights. You can now ask Gemini to broadcast a message and follow up with a reply message in separate commands. Recently, Google Home rolled out a fix for users having problems with their smart lights. The bug caused lights to turn on or off without input from the user. With that issue in the rearview mirror, Google is now rolling out a Gemini for Home update designed to grant you better control over your lights. This update will also improve Spotify media selection and make broadcasting messages easier. Starting with your smart lights, Google announced that Gemini for Home will now let you set specific color temperatures with your voice. For example, you could say. “Hey Google, make the living room lights 2700 kelvins.” With this function, Google aims to make it easier to use your voice to set the mood in your home.

title: Google Home now works better with a wider range of smart locks
summary: Smart locks with both bolts and latches are now more compatible.
body: TL;DR Google has detailed the latest updates for Google Home. Improvements include better support for mortise locks and a fix for a camera bug that caused streams to get stuck at 360p. All these improvements are available now. Google Home is fixing some niche smart home annoyances. Google’s shared update notes for the latest additions to its smart home platform, and changes include a fix for video streaming resolution issues, as well as improved support for what Google calls European-style smart locks. Google posted the release notes for the latest changes on the Google Home and Nest Help forum today. As of this month, the Home platform better supports European-style smart locks, also known as mortise locks. A bug that’s been causing live camera feeds to stream at a locked resolution of 360p has also been addressed.
